nexusClaim.associationBasis: Authoring registers this relationship only as the association the located stress-fracture literature supports. A 2016 narrative review of high-risk stress fractures identifies a subset of injuries with a greater risk of fracture progression, delayed healing and nonunion — the femoral neck (tension side), patella, anterior tibia, medial malleolus, talus, tarsal navicular, proximal fifth metatarsal and great-toe sesamoids — sharing a characteristic region of high tensile load and low blood flow, and requiring more aggressive evaluation and often surgical treatment, while stating that stress fractures overall have an excellent prognosis with little risk of complication (PMID 26972260); and a 2021 systematic review of 13 studies and 393 proximal-fifth-metatarsal stress fractures (pooled mean follow-up 52.5 months; methodological quality assessed as low; Level IV) quantifies the adverse-healing outcomes by treatment modality: pooled bone union 87 percent (95 percent CI 83-90) after surgical treatment versus 56 percent (41-70) after non-surgical treatment, radiological union 13.1 versus 20.9 weeks, delayed union 3 percent (1-5) versus 0 percent (0-8), nonunion 4 percent (2-6) versus 33 percent (20-47), and refracture 7 percent (4-10) versus 12 percent (5-24), with the authors stating the non-surgical evidence is limited by underreporting (PMID 33615403). The registered claim is the narrowest these anchors jointly permit: stress fractures — particularly at the named high-risk sites — are associated with impaired bone healing (delayed union, nonunion, refracture), with the quantification located for the proximal fifth metatarsal only and with the treatment-modality contrast carrying the selection effects its design cannot remove.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of malunion or nonunion is established for any individual by these anchors, and the outcome is measured as progression of the SAME injury rather than a separately caused disease. The narrative review supplies the site-based risk framing without denominators or comparison, its stated overall prognosis for stress fractures is excellent with little risk of complication, and the systematic review's per-modality figures are stratified by the treatment actually received, so the surgical-versus-non-surgical differences (87 versus 56 percent union; 4 versus 33 percent nonunion) reflect which fractures were selected for which management rather than a property of the stress fracture alone; the review's own non-surgical evidence is limited by underreporting (return-to-pre-injury-sport time reported for 6 non-surgically treated fractures against 117 surgical). No located anchor measures malunion specifically, quantifies an individual's healing trajectory, or separates intrinsic site biology from re-injury, return-to-loading timing and treatment choice. Individual claims require a documented stress fracture at a named site with its diagnostic imaging and grade, a dated treatment and loading history, serial imaging or examination establishing delayed or failed union (and, for any malunion reading, union in non-anatomic position), and exclusion of re-injury, infection, metabolic bone disease, medication effects, and alternative pathology (bone cyst, tumor, osteomyelitis) before any attribution.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized local bone-repair failure pathway: at the high-risk sites the injured bone shares a region of high tensile load and comparatively low blood flow, so reparative callus is exposed to repetitive tensile strain while the perfusion needed to consolidate it is limited, which is held to produce delayed union, nonunion and refracture; the located review's union-time contrast (13.1 versus 20.9 weeks) and the high non-surgical nonunion rate are consistent with a site- and loading-dependent reparative limit, but no anchor measures the mechanism directly and treatment selection confounds the modality contrast, so the route is stated as hypothesized rather than established.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Treatment modality, post-injury loading and return-to-activity timing are independent determinants that the located evidence measures as outcomes of the management decision rather than of the stress fracture itself, and the anchors do not separate those operational factors from intrinsic site biology.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on one narrative review and one systematic review and deliberately not beyond them. The located evidence establishes that a high-risk stress-fracture subset carries greater risk of fracture progression, delayed healing and nonunion (femoral neck tension side, patella, anterior tibia, medial malleolus, talus, tarsal navicular, proximal fifth metatarsal, great-toe sesamoids; PMID 26972260) and quantifies adverse healing for one of those sites: 13 studies and 393 proximal-fifth-metatarsal fractures showing 87 percent union after surgical treatment versus 56 percent after non-surgical treatment, nonunion 4 versus 33 percent, delayed union 3 versus 0 percent, refracture 7 versus 12 percent, at Level IV with methodological quality assessed as low (PMID 33615403). Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the outcome is the same injury failing to heal rather than a second disease; the modality contrast is a treatment comparison subject to selection; the narrative review's own overall prognosis statement (stress fractures generally have an excellent prognosis with little risk of complication) bounds the claim; the anchors never measure malunion; and the batch-95 screen did not locate a third site-specific outcome anchor, so the multi-site statement rests on the narrative review alone. All references remain unverified pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; this suggestion, its registry lockstep and its adjacency node landed together on 2026-10-04 as batch 95 of the D1 draft-authoring series.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Anchor-tier and coverage: only two anchors were located — a narrative review supplying the multi-site high-risk framing without outcome quantification (PMID 26972260) and one systematic review whose pooled outcomes cover the proximal fifth metatarsal ONLY (PMID 33615403) — and no third site-specific outcome anchor was located in the batch-95 screen. Design limits: the systematic review is Level IV with methodological quality assessed as low, uses a simplified pooling technique across mostly small non-randomized series, and states that its non-surgical evidence is limited by underreporting (return-to-pre-injury-sport time reported for 6 non-surgically treated fractures against 117 surgical). Treatment-selection confounding: the union, nonunion and refracture figures are stratified by the treatment actually received, so the surgical-versus-non-surgical differences reflect which fractures were selected for which management and cannot be read as treatment effects or as a property of the stress fracture alone. No malunion-specific outcome: the anchors measure delayed union, nonunion and refracture; no located anchor measures malunion, so the registered evidence covers part of the umbrella target identity only. No individual-level trajectory: no anchor reports how many stress fractures progress to nonunion per individual follow-up, quantifies stress-fracture grade or site-specific exposure for any individual, or separates intrinsic site biology from re-injury, return-to-loading timing and treatment choice.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Normal healing-timeline variation: the located surgical cohort still required 13.1 weeks to radiological union and 56 percent of non-surgically treated fractures united, so a slow-healing but progressing fracture is not a nonunion
Re-injury or premature return to loading rather than a failure of intrinsic biology, which the located anchors do not separate from site factors

Treatment effects and treatment-selection: the modality contrast (87 versus 56 percent union; 4 versus 33 percent nonunion) reflects which fractures were selected for surgery, and surgical complications such as infection or hardware failure are treatment consequences rather than secondary conditions

Alternative intrinsic healing impairments documented in the individual record: vitamin D deficiency, hypogonadism, diabetes, smoking, alcohol use, thyroid disease, nutritional deficiency, and medication effects (corticosteroids, NSAIDs, fluoroquinolones)

Alternative pathology at the same site presenting as a non-healing lesion — bone cysts, bone tumors, osteomyelitis or malignancy — which are the target identity's other registered incoming windows and must be excluded by imaging and, where indicated, histology
Misclassification of the original injury (an acute or low-risk fracture misdiagnosed as a stress fracture), altering the expected healing trajectory

sourceReferences.citation: McInnis KC, Ramey LN. High-Risk Stress Fractures: Diagnosis and Management. PM R. 2016 Mar;8(3 Suppl):S113-24. doi:10.1016/j.pmrj.2015.09.019. PMID 26972260.
sourceReferences.note: Narrative review of high-risk stress fractures, registered as this edge's SITE-RISK anchor: it names the high-risk subset with a greater risk of fracture progression, delayed healing and nonunion — femoral neck (tension side), patella, anterior tibia, medial malleolus, talus, tarsal navicular, proximal fifth metatarsal and great-toe sesamoids — and identifies the shared characteristic of high tensile load and low blood flow, while stating that stress fractures in athletes overall have an excellent prognosis for return to sport with little risk of complication. Registered FOR THE RISK FRAMING ONLY: the review reports no union, nonunion or refracture rates, no denominators and no comparison group, and its clinical guidance (imaging, immobilization, surgical referral) is management advice rather than outcome evidence. Its overall-prognosis statement is carried on the edge as the calibration counterweight against over-reading the high-risk subset. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source enters verified:false pending separate qualified-human citation review.

sourceReferences.note: Systematic review of 13 studies and 393 proximal-fifth-metatarsal stress fractures (pooled mean follow-up 52.5 months; MINORS methodological assessment; simplified pooling across mostly small non-randomized series; Level IV), registered as this edge's QUANTIFIED-OUTCOME anchor: union 87 percent (95 percent CI 83-90) after surgical versus 56 percent (41-70) after non-surgical treatment; radiological union 13.1 versus 20.9 weeks; delayed union 3 percent (1-5) versus 0 percent (0-8); nonunion 4 percent (2-6) versus 33 percent (20-47); refracture 7 percent (4-10) versus 12 percent (5-24); return to sport at any level 100 percent in both arms. LIMITATIONS CARRIED: outcomes are stratified by treatment received, so modality differences reflect selection rather than treatment effects; methodological quality assessed as low; non-surgical evidence limited by underreporting (return-to-pre-injury-sport time for 6 non-surgically treated fractures against 117 surgical); and outcomes cover ONE of the named high-risk sites, not the multi-site claim. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source enters verified:false pending separate qualified-human citation review.
